messages:
Ali: Heads up — bringing up HF->Redwood conversion for ghz-13b today. Streaming answers are getting truncated early when the model emits repeated EOS markers. Seen it twice on dev and once in canary.
Mateo: ugh. Can you paste the converter config + a short example of the stream output? Does HF tokenizer have multiple eos variants or special_tokens_map weirdness?
Ali: snippet from config.json we used:
```json
{
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "pad_token": "<|pad|>",
  "special_tokens_map": {"eos_token": "</s>"},
  "chat": {"stop_sequences": ["</s>", "\n\n"]}
}
```
Ali: example user prompt and streaming chunks (raw token text):
USER: "Summarize the doc"
STREAM CHUNK 1: "Sure — here's a short summary."
STREAM CHUNK 2: "</s>\n</s>"  <-- client-side stream closed right after this, payload truncated.
Mateo: hmm those consecutive `</s>` are suspicious. HF tokenizers sometimes emit multiple eos pieces if decode/normalization differs or if detokenization merges separators. Did you run `tokenizer.encode(..., add_special_tokens=True)` vs False?
Priya: Also check the chat template: stop_sequences with both `</s>` and "\n\n" can interfere — if runtime treats any matched stop as immediate termination, consecutive eos could be interpreted as two separate stops leading to an early flush. :thinking_face:
Ali: I tried `add_special_tokens=True` and False — behavior changes. With True I sometimes see one `</s>`, with False the model emits `</s>` plus an extra empty token that we end up converting to `</s>` again in postproc.
Priya: Could be a tokenizer vs postprocessing mismatch in the HF->Redwood conversion layer. Two concrete checks:
- Verify `tokenizer.all_special_tokens` and `tokenizer.special_tokens_map` after loading model + tokenizer.
- Inspect the converter's `chat.stop_sequences` normalization step — we should canonicalize to token ids and dedupe adjacent identical tokens before streaming.
Mateo: runtime-bot just reported a canary change earlier today that modified stop-handling semantics: `treat_stop_as_eos = true` was flipped for canary to test fallbacks. @runtime-bot can you paste deploy id?
runtime-bot: deploy 2026-03-18_09:12 - canary flag `treat_stop_as_eos=true` on 3 hosts.
Mateo: that matches timeline. If the runtime now treats stop tokens as hard termination, a doubled eos in the stream could trigger an extra state transition and close the stream. We should make stop matching idempotent for consecutive identical tokens.
Ali: Proposed short-term mitigation: collapse consecutive identical tokens during decode before emitting a stop event. Quick code sketch I used locally:
```python
# pseudo
out_tokens = []
for t in streamed_token_ids:
    if not out_tokens or t != out_tokens[-1]:
        out_tokens.append(t)
# then run stop_match(out_tokens)
```
Priya: That's reasonable for a patch. Long-term we should: 1) ensure converter writes canonical `eos_token_id` into model config.json, 2) add unit tests for streaming with sequences like `[eos, eos, eos]`, `[eos, newline, eos]`, and quantized variants.
Mateo: Agreed. Also add a small eval that compares HF decode vs Redwood decode on the same token stream to catch mapping drift. Could be part of the model onboarding checklist. :white_check_mark:
Ali: I'll open a ticket and push a quick canary fix to dedupe stops at emit-time. Patch will include the unit test Priya suggested. Ticket: RG-1452 (will link to PR).
Priya: Nice. Also watch for padding tokens sneaking in — if pad_token_id == eos_token_id in any quantized conversion, that'll cause spurious stops. Add an assert in conversion step: `pad_id != eos_id` or remap pad to a reserved id.
Ali: Good call. I'll add both checks + a tiny reproducer so QA can hit it with streaming clients. Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
